26 Which statement concerning a stationary wave is correct?
A
All the particles between two adjacent nodes oscillate in phase.
B
The amplitude of the stationary wave is equal to the amplitude of one of the waves creating it.
C
The wavelength of the stationary wave is equal to the separation of two adjacent nodes.
D
There is no displacement of a particle at an antinode at any time.

hints: Focus on the meanings of node with zero vibration and antinode with maximum vibration in a stationary wave.
Recall that one loop between two adjacent nodes moves up and down together, but the loop on the other side of a node moves oppositely.
Compare node separation with wavelength using $\text{node to node} = \lambda/2$ and compare antinode amplitude with the amplitude of one travelling wave.
walkthrough: Recall a stationary wave is formed by two progressive waves of the same frequency and amplitude travelling in opposite directions.
Nodes are points of destructive superposition with zero amplitude at all times, and antinodes are points of constructive superposition with maximum oscillation.

Between two adjacent nodes all particles move in the same direction at the same time and pass through equilibrium together, so they are in phase with each other. Phase reverses only when crossing a node.
Check the wavelength rule: two adjacent nodes enclose one loop, which is half a wave pattern, so separation $= \lambda/2$, not $\lambda$.
Check the amplitude and antinode rules: the antinode amplitude is the sum of the two creating amplitudes, equal to $2A$, and an antinode particle has maximum displacement, not zero displacement.
Therefore only the statement about particles between two adjacent nodes oscillating in phase follows. This is option A.

A.explanation: All particles in one loop between two adjacent nodes reach maximum displacement and zero together, so they vibrate in phase.

B.explanation: At an antinode the two creating waves reinforce, so the maximum amplitude is twice the amplitude of one creating wave.

C.explanation: The separation of two adjacent nodes is only half a wavelength, so $\text{node separation} = \lambda/2$.

D.explanation: It is a node that has zero displacement at all times, while an antinode oscillates with maximum amplitude.
